Our approach to the services we provide is holistic and grounded in a public health model, starting at birth, providing children with monthly books up to age 5, and helping foster youth with savings accounts as they transition to adulthood. jobs.title: Lead Integrated Community Supports Housing Navigator
jobs.description:
The Lead Integrated Community Supports (ICS) Housing Navigator provides housing\-focused case management services through the Behavioral Health Bridge Housing (BHBH) Program and utilizes California Advancing and Innovating Medi\-Cal (CalAIM) service activities where eligible. This position serves BHSA\-eligible clients placed in interim housing with the goal of securing and transitioning clients into permanent, stable housing. The Housing Navigator collaborates with behavioral health staff, county partners, and community providers to address housing barriers and deliver comprehensive, recovery\-oriented support.



Essential Job Duties:



Housing Navigation \& Placement


* Conduct outreach and engage clients in interim housing to assess housing needs and establish service relationships.


* Complete housing assessments and develop individualized Housing Action Plans in collaboration with the client and BHBH team.


* Identify and secure permanent housing opportunities, including navigating waiting lists, completing applications, and coordinating move\-in logistics.


* Advocate on behalf of clients with landlords, property managers, and housing authorities to overcome barriers related to rental history, credit, or prior evictions.


* Connect clients to rental assistance, subsidies, and benefits programs (e.g., GR, SSI/SSDI, Medi\-Cal) to support housing affordability and sustainability.



Client Support \& Case Management


* As eligible, provide ongoing ICS housing support across all elements of available CalAIM community supports, including Navigation, Deposit assistance, Transitional rent and Tenancy Sustaining services.


* Transport clients to housing\-related appointments as needed; coordinate with the care team to address barriers to engagement.


* Use a Housing First, Trauma\-Informed, and Harm Reduction approach in all client interactions.


* Assist clients in understanding lease obligations, maintaining unit conditions, and building relationships with landlords and neighbors.


* Coach clients on budgeting, household management, and accessing community resources to promote long\-term housing stability.



Care Coordination \& Collaboration


* Collaborate with BHBH behavioral health staff, county case managers, and community partners to ensure integrated, person\-centered service delivery.


* Participate in case conferencing and multidisciplinary team meetings to coordinate care planning and problem\-solve housing barriers.


* Coordinate warm handoffs and transitional support as clients move from interim to permanent housing.


* Represent the program at county\-wide housing and community meetings as required.



Documentation \& Compliance


* Complete accurate and timely documentation in compliance with county requirements, BHSA program standards, and DHCS/CalAIM policy guidelines.


* Enter and maintain data in HMIS, SPRITE, and other required MCP, county and agency databases.


* Record case notes, housing action plans, service contacts, and outcome data in accordance with program policies.


* Support Medi\-Cal billing processes by ensuring documentation meets ICS service requirements and timelines.



Supervisor Support/ Team Leadership


* Support Supervisors in ensuring services are delivered in a professional manner in accordance with all departmental and organizational policies and procedures


* Support supervisors with administration and reporting.


* Professionally represent City Net at all collaborative meetings.


* Ensure openings are occupied in a timely manner and oversee unit readiness.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS


* One (1\) year of experience in case management, housing navigation, or a related human services role.


* Experience working with individuals with serious mental illness, substance use disorders, or other disabling conditions.


* Familiarity with CalAIM, BHSA eligibility, or Medi\-Cal\-funded services preferred.


* Experience with county documentation systems and/or HMIS preferred.


* Valid California driver's license, personal vehicle with current registration and insurance.

  

SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE \& ABILITIES


* Knowledge of Housing First, Trauma\-Informed Care, and Harm Reduction principles.


* Familiarity with Orange County social services systems, including Medi\-Cal, CalOptima, GR, Social Security, and community behavioral health providers.


* Understanding of CalAIM Integrated Community Supports (ICS) services and county documentation requirements.


* Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple clients and deadlines in a fast\-paced environment.


* Effective written and verbal communication skills.


* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams) and web\-based databases.


* Collaborative team player with strong interpersonal and conflict resolution skills.


* Commitment to ending homelessness and serving individuals with complex needs.

  

ENVIRONMENTAL \& PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS



This is a field\-based position. Work is performed in community settings including interim housing sites (hotels/motels), client homes, county offices, and in the field. Employees must be able to spend significant time standing, walking, and driving. The ability to lift and/or push up to 25 pounds may be required. Use of a personal vehicle for client transportation and community appointments is required.

**PAY:** *$3,116/month Full Time, $1,558/month Part Time*

**Make a difference in the lives of others!** The AmeriCorps Partnership, a program of NSBC United Way, is recruiting AmeriCorps members to support homeless folk and veterans throughout the Central Coast

Positions begin **SEPTEMBER 14, 2026** and the contract runs to **AUGUST 31, 2026**

**Overview**

We are seeking an energetic and compassionate Housing Navigator to join our AmeriCorps team. In this vital role, you will serve as a key connector for individuals and families facing housing instability, guiding them through the complex landscape of housing options and support programs. Your efforts will help empower underserved populations to attain and maintain stable housing, while strengthening local partnerships and community resources.

You will be matched with one of the following Partners:

***Department of Social Services***

*Roles and responsibilities of members include:*

* Contact applicants and conduct intake interviews/assessment.
* Enter information into California automated Welfare System (Cal SAWS), as well as the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS)
* Conduct face to face interviews with applicants for Immediate Need (IN) and or Expedited Services (ES) to assess risk of homelessness.
* Scan documentation into Cal SAWS imaging system – Hyland
* Conduct home visits to assess the habitability of potential housing for our clients, and determine the level of assistance needed to make home habitable (furniture, bedding, etc.)
* Other duties as assigned based on departmental needs when serving population at risk/or experiencing homelessness

***Housing Authority of the County of Santa Barbara***

*Roles and responsibilities of members include:*

* Coordinating services for clients in need of resources and benefits including Medi\-Cal and Medicare, housing applications, and food security programs
* Facilitating mental health counseling, financial literacy education, job readiness, and life skills workshops for recently housed beneficiaries
* Facilitating the “document readiness” process to prepare beneficiary applications for housing
* Enrolling beneficiaries in the Homeless Management Information System
* Collaborating with community partners on housing retention activities
* Street outreach in Santa Barbara County
* Volunteer recruitment and management

***Public Defender's Office***

*Roles and responsibilities of members include:*

* Connecting clients to benefits such as Cal fresh, General Relief, Social Security, etc.
* Connecting clients to outpatient and mental health services
* Transporting clients to appointments
* Assisting clients in getting into shelters and transitional housing.
* Seeking resources to assist clients with their needs.
* Building rapport with other agencies and providers in collaborating to assist client’s need as a team.
* Advocating for clients in court while also connecting clients to benefits and resources.
* Tabling community events

***YMCA Haley Street Navigation Center***

*Roles and responsibilities of members include:*

* Perform street\-based outreach, walking/traveling specified routes to locate and engage with at\-risk youth to offer supportive services and immediate resources.
* Support a warm, welcoming, and inclusive environment at the drop\-in center, assist youth with basic needs, support services, and appropriate referrals.
* Utilize program assessments and screening tools in collaboration with each youth to inform priorities of the individual service plan and make appropriate internal and external referrals for services.
* Support youth to enhance their education, vocation, relationships and communication, independent living skills, physical health, mental health, and more.
* Ensure client records and documentation are accurate, up\-to\-date, and confidential.
* Support the daily collection and tracking of statistical data to be used for completing programmatic required reports.
* Assist with housing navigation, search, and landlord recruitment efforts.
* Maintain working knowledge of local community resources and provide youth with referrals to other agencies for services when appropriate

***NSBC United Way Home For Good***

*Roles and responsibilities of members include:*

* Case management for clients in need of resources and benefits including health care, housing applications, food banks, mental health services, and employment assistance
* Utilizing a “document readiness” process to prepare beneficiary applications for housing
* Enrolling beneficiaries in the Homeless Management Information System at Coordinated Entry System access points
* Facilitating community education programs that improve career readiness, financial literacy, and life skills
* Assisting with Cal\-AIM programming
* Street outreach in the Central Coast
* Volunteer recruitment and management

**The agencies above focus on mental health services, criminal justice advocacy, housing acquisition/retention, and general social services.**

Members serve as a part of AmeriCorps, a network of national service programs that supports 75,000 members across the country each year. Members are assigned to one of a variety of non\-profit and public agency partners for their term of service.

***VOALA***

The Care Coordinator supports survivors of domestic violence and Missing and Murdered Indigenous People (MMIP)\-affected families by connecting them with essential services and resources. This position coordinates referrals, facilitates access to mental health and victim support services, and assists individuals in crisis. The Care Coordinator also engages with the community to strengthen prevention services and supports the development of outreach efforts to raise awareness of MMIP\-related issues.

**Pay Range:** $50,000\-$78,000 PER YR


**Reporting To:** HCBA Lead Intake Case Manager/Program Manager


**Work Type:** Remote/ Field Work

  


**POSITION SUMMARY:**


The Intake Case Manager manages and maintains their caseload, provides case management services to each of their applicant clients or caregivers on an ongoing basis until or shortly thereafter the applicant is enrolled in the HCBA waiver.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS:**


* Master’s Degree in Social Work or Bachelors degree in related field.


* Minimum of two years of experience providing direct mental health or intensive case management.


* Experience working with clients with mental illness, or chronic health issues.


* Proficient knowledge of managed care organizations, Medicare, and Medi\-Cal


* Excellent interpersonal skills and sensitivity to working with culturally diverse populations.


* Well\-organized and able to comply with documentation and reporting requirements.


* Ability to maintain professional boundaries with clients and effectively manage time.


* Current CPR certification.

* Case Manager is assigned a case load of which they support the client during the enrollment process.

**Development Coordinator**### **Overview of the Position**


The Development Coordinator serves as the operational backbone of SEAL’s Development \& External Relations team and reports to the Head Development and External Relations Officer. This role ensures fundraising, grant development, donor cultivation, communications, business development, and strategic initiatives move forward efficiently through proactive project management, operational excellence, and precise digital systems management. Collaborating across multiple departments, the coordinator manages timelines, oversees project workflows, maintains Salesforce and other development systems, supports donor and grant operations, and continuously improves the processes that enable SEAL to scale its impact.  

This position is ideal for someone who thrives on bringing structure to complex projects, enjoys improving systems, embraces technology, and takes pride in helping teams succeed.  

This hybrid position is based in California. You will work from home and in the field, with the expectation to travel 5\-15% throughout the year.### **About SEAL**


For more than 15 years, SEAL has worked with school districts, county offices of education, schools, preschool LEAs, teachers, families, California Department of Education, and many other education champions to advance educational outcomes of English Learners and Dual Language Learners. It all began with Dr. Laurie Olsen and Sobrato Philanthropies whose strong belief that all children should have access to opportunities for growth and success led to designing, piloting and eventually creating the SEAL you know today.  

Our vision at SEAL is simple, yet impactful: schools prepare all English Learners and Dual Language Learners to learn, lead and thrive. Our core values focus on nurturing the intellectual and linguistic brilliance of young children, celebrating the importance of family culture and language in education, and supporting teachers through professional development and evidence\-based instructional practices.  

We work across California and nationally, partnering with preschools, elementary schools, districts, county offices and other educational stakeholders to ensure culturally and linguistically diverse children thrive. Extensive research has shown that SEAL both enhances teaching methods and leads to higher engagement and improved language and academic results among English Learners and Dual Language Learners. We’ve impacted hundreds of classrooms, thousands of teachers, tens of thousands of students—and counting. The number of school districts successfully implementing SEAL grows each year.  

SEAL addresses systemic inequities by transforming classrooms into joyful, rigorous, and language\-affirming environments. Our Theory of Action drives impact across three integrated levels:* **Direct Impact:** Building the capacity of teachers and leaders through specialized professional learning.
* **Ecosystem Impact:** Partnering with education organizations to embed MLL expertise into programs, tools, and training.
* **Field Impact:** Leading advocacy and awareness to elevate high\-quality instructional practices at scale.

  

To learn more about SEAL, please visit SEAL.org**.**

### **Our Equity Commitment**


Equity is a core value at SEAL. At SEAL, our commitment to diversity, equity \& inclusion reflects SEAL's mission: "To Prepare All English Learners to learn, thrive, and lead." We believe that non\-profit organizations can be powerful platforms for social change and that our higher purpose is to drive equity for all.### **About the Role**

The Book Club of California is a nonprofit member and donor supported organization dedicated to preserving and promoting the history of the book and the books arts. The Book Club hosts book\-related exhibitions, a year\-round series of public programs, and publishes limited edition books, keepsakes, and the letterpress\-printed *Quarterly News\-Letter*. A special collections library is dedicated to supporting and preserving the book arts, as well as the history and literature of the West. **RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE PROGRAM COORDINATOR**

The Program Coordinator works collaboratively with the Executive Director, staff, and the Programs Committee to identify, develop, and execute programs including talks, exhibitions, field trips, and book\-related events for the membership and public; and produce and develop publicity and marketing materials for programs, publications, and other organizational initiatives.

The Program Coordinator is a non\-exempt, part\-time (24 hours/week) position with standard hours, typically Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 10am\-6pm. On Monday evenings when public programs are held the hours would typically be 12pm\-8pm. Additional evening or weekend hours may be required based on committee meetings and other activities. “In\-office hours” are negotiable/flexible, as some work can be done remotely, while other responsibilities are based in the office. The Program Coordinator must reside in the Bay Area since a portion of the work must be done on\-sight at the Book Club.

* Schedule and execute programs including coordinating event logistics (securing venues, reservation system, speaker A/V requirements, volunteer staffing, etc.) and marketing/outreach (social media, email, print)

* Monitor event details, collect attendee information and presenter surveys, and other reporting

* Maintain program listings and reservation systems on website, Zoom, etc.
* Manage organizational email communications related to programs and publications

* Collaborate with Executive Director and staff to execute a strategic communications plan to advance the organization’s mission, goals, and objectives

* Support a culture of philanthropy and promote membership and volunteerism

**RN On Site Care Coordinator Position Summary**  

The On\-site Care Coordinator is a Registered Nurse who provides care coordination, education and outreach services on\-site (various locations including home) to Medicaid members in the Medically Complex Children’s Waiver program. This position requires licensure as a Registered Nurse in the State of SC.


**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**  

* Upon referral, perform an initial medical eligibility assessment to determine eligibility for the program. If qualified, perform an initial, in\-home, level of care assessment to include the completion of all required documentation.
* Fulfills requirements established by SCDHHS to complete an annual home visit, three in person quarterly visits, and monthly contact calls during months a visit is not required. Ensuring the information contained in the system of record is accurate and complete.
* Provides members and their authorized representatives with education required to care for members and arranges appropriate education services, if necessary.
* Develops case specific care plans/service plans and presents to the primary care provider for approval and/or revision; submits care plan to DHHS for approval.
* Collaborate with the Care Advocate Team to ensure all required services, communications, documentation, and ancillary needs are addressed. Maintains availability to members, their authorized representatives, and providers to coordinate any required services.
* Serve as a member advocate, attending educational advocacy meetings, team conferences, etc. as requested and available. Addresses and identifies complaints, grievances, or concerns and escalates to the appropriate stakeholder, when necessary.
* Develops disaster plan, identifies availability of advanced directives, needs for ancillary services, specialty services and community services.
* Upon member ineligibility, age out, or other circumstance in which disenrollment from the program becomes necessary, complete all needed activities to ensure continuation of care and communicate with all stakeholders to ensure an uninterrupted transition of care.
* Serve as a mandated reporter.
* Will have access and manage PHI in accordance with federal and state requirements (HIPAA, HITECH).
  

**Supervisory Responsibilities**  

N/A

  

**Competencies:**  

* Strong organizational, interpersonal and motivational skills
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Detail oriented
* High level of reasoning and analytical skills
* Ability to multi\-task and work independently

**Qualifications:**  

* A Minimum of three (3\) years of recent clinical pediatric experience is required.
* A bachelor’s degree in a health\-related field is strongly preferred.
* Previous work experience with a Medicaid program is preferred.
* Bilingual (Spanish) is preferred.
* Ability to travel locally with a valid drivers’ license and automobile insurance
* Initial TB negative test and completion of a TB questionnaire, yearly
  

**Certificates, Licenses, Registrations:**  

* A Bachelor’s degree in a health related field is strongly preferred.
* A minimum of three (3\) years of Pediatric Nursing, Pediatric Home Care experience is premium
* Certified Case Management (CCM) Certification is preferred
* Current RN licensure in states where business is conducted.
* Current BLS certification
  

**Computer Skills:**  

Demonstrated computer proficiency with all Microsoft 365 products, electronic health record (EHR/EMR) systems, clinical data entry, telehealth platforms, Medicaid documentation and care management platforms, and the ability to efficiently navigate multiple electronic systems while maintaining accurate, timely, and compliant clinical documentation in accordance with state and regulatory requirements.

  

**Environmental Factors/Physical Demands**  

This position is primarily performed from a remote home office and requires periodic travel to patients' homes and other assigned locations. The employee is responsible for maintaining a professional, safe, and secure home workspace with reliable high\-speed internet access that supports the secure handling of confidential and protected health information (PHI). Employees are responsible for providing and maintaining their own home office furniture and workspace.

  



While performing the essential functions of this position, the employee will regularly use a computer, telephone, and other office equipment; communicate with patients, caregivers, providers, and team members through various electronic platforms; and enter, retrieve, and maintain information in multiple electronic health record (EHR) and Medicaid documentation systems. The position requires prolonged periods of sitting, keyboarding, and viewing computer monitors.

  



Periodic travel is required to conduct patient home visits and attend meetings or training as assigned. The employee must be able to safely operate a motor vehicle, enter and exit patient residences, and occasionally navigate uneven walkways, stairs, or other environmental conditions encountered during home visits.



The position may require standing, walking, bending, reaching, kneeling, stooping, and lifting or carrying materials and equipment weighing up to thirty (30\) pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

  


**Other Responsibilities**  

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.  

* Adheres to the policies and procedures of South Carolina Solutions
* Maintains strict confidentiality of client, company and personnel information
* Demonstrates a strong commitment to the mission and values of the organization
* Adheres to company attendance standards
*

As a national leader in value\-based care, we offer senior living communities and skilled nursing facilities a wide range of solutions (including on\-site primary care services, Accountable Care Organizations, and Medicare Advantage Special Needs Plans) proven to enhance health outcomes, streamline operations, and create new financial opportunities.

Ranked \#147 on the Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest\-growing private companies, we're just getting started. If you're looking to make a meaningful impact on the senior healthcare landscape, you're in the right place—and we look forward to working with you.  

For more information about our company, visit CuranaHealth.com. To learn more about our health plan offerings please visit alignseniorcare.com.  


**Summary**
-----------

At Curana Health, we know that care is more than clinical checklists—it is about truly seeing and supporting the whole person. As a Care Ally Case Manager, you will be the trusted connection point between our members, their families, care teams, and our internal partners. You will guide, advocate, and coordinate care so that every member feels heard, cared for, and supported in living their healthiest life.

  


**Essential Duties \& Responsibilities**
----------------------------------------

**Responsibilities**

* Be the bridge: Serve as the go\-to liaison between members, families/POAs, providers, and the Align Senior Care team.
* Assess \& plan holistically: Conduct comprehensive health assessments, create personalized care plans, and participate in interdisciplinary team meetings to ensure members’ needs are met.
* Coach \& educate: Act as a health coach—empowering members and families with knowledge about conditions, treatment plans, benefits, and community resources.
* Support daily needs: Help members navigate appointments, medications, supplemental benefits, and transitions between care settings.

* You’ll play a key role in shaping member experience and bringing Curana Health's mission to life.

* Proficiency using basic computer skills in Microsoft Office such as Word, Excel, and Outlook, including the ability to navigate multiple systems and keyboarding.

* Bilingual in Spanish preferred
